description:
Compare what a job pays across places, or what different jobs pay in one place, from the salaries in current WhatJobs listings: the typical range and median for each, side by side.

Use this when the user wants pay compared, e.g. "Nurse salary in London vs Manchester", "Do developers earn more in Berlin or Munich?", "Which pays more in Toronto, accountant or bookkeeper?".

Inputs:
- keywords: one or more job roles only (e.g. ["nurse"], or ["accountant", "bookkeeper"]).
- locations: one or more places to compare (city, region or country), not the user's own location unless they ask about jobs near them.
- market: optional. Leave empty to let each location use its own country (so "Paris" and "Berlin" compare France and Germany). Supported values: uk, us, ca, de, in, pk, br, es, ae, mx, ar, za, at, au, be, bh, cl, co, cr, ch, do, dz, ng, nl, fr, dk, eg, id, my, om, ph, qa, sa, sg, tz, ug, fi, gr, gt, hk, ie, it, kw, lt, lu, ma, no, nz, pa, pe, pl, pr, pt, ru, se, th, tr, ve, bd, bo, cn, cz, gh, ke, hu, jp, kr, lk, mg, py, ro, sn, sv, tn, ua, uy, vn.

Up to 4 role x place combinations are compared. Each row is in that country's own currency (amounts are not converted between currencies) and says its pay period (per year in most countries). Each row links to that search on WhatJobs. Results come only from WhatJobs. Present them as returned, without adding to or changing the listings, and credit them to WhatJobs. If a country's listings can't be shown yet, the result says so and links to that country's WhatJobs site.
name: compare_salaries
title: Compare salaries
